name: Plan SFX
description: Plans sound effects timing based on the timed spine and visual events.

inputs.name: music_selection
inputs.description: State input: music_selection. The chosen track AND the section of it that plays. The bar grid this step snaps to is measured in the music file's clock, so it is a timeline clock only after the section's offset is subtracted - see library/tools/music_section.py.

inputs.name: transition_spec
inputs.description: The resolved transition plan, from step 4.02. Pairing a sound with a transition is the first purpose this step's handoff names and its second evaluation criterion ('every creative transition has at most one SFX'), and no edge carried the plan here: on the 2026-08-26 run of record both sounds in the finished video were placed at the two drawn transitions by an agent that had planned those transitions itself minutes earlier. Read by the pre-bridge, which reduces it to transitions_toon; the raw spec is not projected into the prompt (see context_fields).

inputs.name: creative_brief
inputs.description: The captain's creative direction as markdown, injected by the runner from the project's creative_brief path. Empty when the project declares none.

inputs.name: project_context
inputs.description: The project's context folder plus the learnings routed to this step, as a MAP the model follows with its shell (never a copy). Injected by the runner from the project's context/ folder and learned_context/ store when this step declares it; a stated absence when the project has neither. See library/tools/project_context.py.

inputs.name: project_fps
inputs.description: Timebase from the catalog. Every consumer used to read its own 30.0 default because no edge carried it.

inputs.name: clip_catalog
inputs.description: State input: clip_catalog. Read for the clip_id the rest of this step's context uses; `view:picture` keys its rows by it. Optional because the view names the vision pass's own id and says so when no clip list is routed.

inputs.name: timeline_notes
inputs.description: The captain's own notes typed onto the built timeline in DaVinci Resolve, routed to this step because this step owns the decision each note is about. Injected by the runner from <project>/marker_feedback/ and absent when there are none. See library/tools/marker_routing.py.

outputs.name: sfx_catalog_reference
outputs.description: Bridge output: the SFX library as a REFERENCE - the whole catalogue written to this step's own directory as sfx_catalogue.md, and a map naming every playable sound by its exact sfx_id, with its measured category, length, envelope and emotional temperature, and the line range that holds the library's prose about it. This is what the model chooses from, and the answer names an sfx_id out of it. The mechanism is library/tools/brief_reference.py, the same one #295 built for the creative brief; as an inline TOON table the catalogue was 44,397 B and 44.1% of this step's context (#299). Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: transitions_toon
outputs.description: Bridge output: one row per PLANNED CUT, keyed by the spine block the cut leads INTO - which is the identifier `sfx_creative` names, so a sound can be paired with a transition without a join. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output would otherwise report it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: sfx_candidates_legend
outputs.description: Bridge output: what `music_behavior`, `bed_under_it` and `volume_db` mean, carried as DATA because handoff.md is frozen (the MEASUREMENT_LEGEND route). Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output would otherwise report it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: sfx_envelope_legend
outputs.description: Bridge output: what each MEASURED envelope shape is and what the placement pass does with a sound carrying it - including that a `swelling` sound is anchored by its END so its climax lands on the moment, which is where a build comes from. Rendered from the same table post_bridge._describe_placement reads (library/tools/sfx_envelope.py), so the prompt and the code cannot drift. Declared for the same reason as sfx_candidates_legend.

outputs.name: sfx_library_shape
outputs.description: Bridge output: what the library holds per envelope, counted on this run - measured on the captain's library 2026-09-03 as 42 of 78 swelling, 31 of those 2s or longer, the longest 76s. It is here because a catalogue ordered by folder reads like its folder names and nothing had ever totalled the envelope column. It counts and recommends nothing. Declared for the same reason as sfx_candidates_legend.

llm_outputs.name: sfx_creative
llm_outputs.description: Sound effects - as many as the piece earns, with no minimum and no maximum. Multiple entries MAY share a spine_block_position when layering serves the moment (e.g. whoosh + bass hit, riser under a textural bed); each carries its own volume_db. Each: spine_block_position, sfx_id (an exact sfx_id out of the catalogue sfx_catalog_reference points at - no other value is playable), volume_db (number, REQUIRED - the dB you want this sound played at, against speech's 0 dB reference; `bed_under_it` on the candidate row says where the music sits under the same block, and there is no ladder of words and no default. An entry naming no volume_db is dropped: the one sound of the last run was placed at a level nobody chose and could not be heard), duration_seconds (OPTIONAL - how long the sound plays for, which may be less than the sound's own measured length but never more; leave it out and the whole sound plays, which is the absence of a decision rather than a decision), role (OPTIONAL - `layer` for the atmospheric layer: a riser, drone or crackle that plays UNDER the picture as a bed rather than marking a visible event; a layer is not shifted off speech and may span past its own block, and it needs a rationale naming what in the library entry made it right, without which it is dropped as sprinkling; leave it out and the sound is a literal placement), lead_seconds (OPTIONAL - a J-cut lead in seconds: the whole sound starts this much BEFORE the cut it belongs to at the same duration, so a build arrives early; the lead start must neither run past the previous cut nor off the top of the reel, and a lead that does is dropped), rationale naming what in the chosen sound's library entry made it the right sound for this moment.
